data.name: Saint Lucia
data.summary: Saint Lucia taxes ordinarily resident individuals on worldwide income (top rate 30%), but capital gains are not taxed and dividends ('distributions from companies') are exempt income by statute. There is no inheritance, gift or net wealth tax. The main residual exposure for a portfolio investor is foreign interest income, which is taxable at up to 30%.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Residents with a permanent place of abode in Saint Lucia are taxed on worldwide income at 15%/20%/30%, but capital gains are not taxed and 'distributions from companies' are exempt income under s. 25 of the Income Tax Act. Foreign interest (other than on Saint Lucian bank deposits) is taxable.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if permanent place of abode in Saint Lucia and present for some time in the year, or present 183 days or more. Non-citizens need a residence permit or citizenship.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains are not taxed. Income from trading in securities 'other than by way of a business' is also listed as exempt income.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Stamp duty on sale of Saint Lucian real property: seller 2.5%-5% (resident) or 10% (non-resident), buyer 2%. Shares of companies with 75%+ real property assets follow real property rates; other share transfers 0.5%.

capital_gains.rate_basis: 0 = no capital gains tax (Deloitte 2026, PwC reviewed 12 Oct 2026); ITA s.25(1)(zs) exempts income from trading in securities other than by way of a business.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Securities trading carried on as a business is outside the s.25(1)(zs) exemption and would be business income taxed at up to 30%.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign gains are not taxed either.

dividends.summary: Dividends ('distributions from companies') are exempt income under ITA s.25(1)(x); Saint Lucia levies no dividend withholding tax. The exemption wording is not limited to Saint Lucian companies.
dividends.important_exceptions: Interest is taxable unless on a deposit in a bank in Saint Lucia (s.25(1)(g)(i)) or another listed exemption; foreign bond interest is taxable at up to 30% for an ordinarily resident individual.

dividends.rate_basis: ITA s.25(1)(x) 'distributions from companies' exempt. PwC confirms dividends from Saint Lucian corporations are exempt; it does not separately discuss foreign dividends, so foreign_gross_rate 0 rests on the statutory wording.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends paid out. Interest and royalties: 10% to residents, 25% to non-residents.
dividends.treaty_network: CARICOM multilateral treaty only; no relief for US/EU source withholding on portfolio dividends.

income.name: Saint Lucia

income_tax.summary: Income tax is 15% on the first XCD 15,000 of taxable income, 20% on the next XCD 15,000 and 30% above, after a XCD 25,000 personal allowance. Employees pay 5% National Insurance up to XCD 5,000 a month.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: UNVERIFIED, derived: no source for the self-employed National Insurance rate could be found (PwC, Deloitte, Hivedesk and Expanship do not give one; the NIC website could not be reached and the US SSA programme page returns 403). 10% equals the combined employee and employer 5% + 5% (PwC confirms the 5% employee share and that the employer matches it), which is how self-employed contributions are normally set in the OECS schemes, but the real figure and any separate self-employed ceiling remain unconfirmed.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income surtax. Residents with a permanent place of abode are taxed on worldwide income; those resident 183+ days without a permanent abode are taxed on Saint Lucia-source income only. Capital gains are not taxed. A 2.5% health and citizen security levy applies on sales of goods and services (not an income tax). Brackets apply to taxable income after the XCD 25,000 allowance; further deductions (mortgage interest up to XCD 40,000, medical, education) exist.

income.residence_routes: No remote-worker programme exists in law: the 'Live It' scheme is a tourism marketing label for the standard visitor entry (up to 6 weeks on arrival, extendable in 30-day steps at EC$200) or a multiple-entry non-immigrant visa (EC$190, 12 months) for nationals who need a visa. Skilled employees of a Saint Lucian employer need a work permit (not researched). Citizenship by investment (National Economic Fund, real estate, bonds) is a separate route; amounts not verified. EU, US and other citizens are treated alike in these routes. US citizens remain taxable in the US on worldwide income.

Work-permit terms and the status of the 'Live It' one-year option not confirmed on an official page.

succession.name: Saint Lucia
succession.summary: Saint Lucia's Civil Code lets an adult dispose of property by will and no reserved share was found. The Code also recognises trusts under English principles. Without a will, a spouse takes one third and the children two thirds. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
succession.foreign_law_note: No source read states Saint Lucia's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate.
succession.trust_note: Not in the HCCH status table. Civil Code art. 916A allows trusts of movable or immovable property, with English law on trustees' duties. The International Trust Act, Cap. 12.19 was repealed with effect from 30 June 2021 (Act 16 of 2018). No private foundation statute was found.
open_questions: Only intestacy arts. 567A-568 and art. 770 were read; absence of a reserved share is inferred, not confirmed.
Revised Laws pages are marked 'not yet authenticated through a Commencement Order'.
Whether any foundation law exists was not confirmed.
Private foundations: no source found either way; not finding a foundation law is not evidence that there is none.

immigration.name: Saint Lucia
immigration.summary: No free movement for anyone. Citizenship by investment starts at USD 240,000 (National Economic Fund), with bonds from USD 300,000 and real estate from USD 300,000. Saint Lucian passports lost UK visa-free access on 5 March 2026. Ordinary residence routes are not sourced from official pages.
immigration.naturalisation: Ordinary naturalisation residence period not verified in this research; see open questions.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Dual citizenship is allowed for CBI citizens (not verified against the Citizenship Act this pass).

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment: National Economic Fund (NEF)
routes.summary: A USD 240,000 non-refundable contribution covers the applicant and up to three dependants.
routes.requirements: USD 240,000 main applicant plus up to 3 dependants; extra dependant under 18 USD 10,000, over 18 USD 20,000. Application processing USD 2,000 main applicant, USD 1,000 per dependant; due diligence USD 8,000 main applicant, USD 5,000 per dependant over 16; interview and identity verification fee for the main applicant. The page links to a July 2024 prices gazette that was not read; figures may be superseded. Banned nationalities not found.
routes.investment_options: NEF USD 240,000; National Action Bonds USD 300,000 (+ USD 50,000 fee, 5-year hold, no interest); real estate USD 300,000 (+ USD 30,000 admin fee for one applicant); enterprise project USD 3,500,000 single / USD 6,000,000 joint, or USD 250,000 under infrastructure option 3.
routes.fees_note: 2,000 processing + 8,000 due diligence for a main applicant; interview fee amount not given.
routes.physical_presence: None stated on the CIP page.
routes.processing_time: Statutory target 90 days; one commercial source reports about 18 months in practice.
routes.tax_note: Citizenship alone does not end tax residence elsewhere.
